title: Scenario Comparator: interactive view for batching & caching cost-latency tradeoffs
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Design an interactive Scenario Comparator panel in the Redwood Console that lets operators and engineers compare up to three configuration scenarios (batching size/policy, prefix cache enabled/ttl, quantization profile) side-by-side. The goal is to make trade-offs between cost per 1k tokens, p99 latency, and token success rate obvious and actionable, and to embed safety guardrail explanations and automatic rollback suggestions for risky configurations.

This ticket covers: low-fidelity flows, high-fidelity prototype, microcopy for guardrails, integration requirements for runtime telemetry, and a short A/B experiment plan for adoption metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype with three-pane comparison exists in Figma and shows cost, latency, and quality metrics for sample workloads
Microcopy for each guardrail state (OK / Caution / Blocked) reviewed and approved by Security and Reliability
Design tokens and component variants provided for Console team (cards, sliders, badges) with accessibility checks
Handoff artifacts include telemetry mapping (metric names + expected granularity) and a minimal API shape for scenario evaluation endpoint
Usability test (5 participants) completed and findings documented with at least 3 concrete changes applied
design_notes: Core interaction: users can create a scenario from an existing route or template, tweak three knobs (batching window / batch size, prefix cache TTL / prefix inclusion filter, model quantization profile), then click Compare to generate simulated metrics based on recent telemetry and model profiles.

Simulation backend: we will initially show model-guided estimations + historical percentiles (p50/p95/p99) instead of real-time synthetic runs to avoid heavy infra demands. Final calculation will be an API call that accepts a scenario JSON and returns metric deltas.

Trade-offs considered: exposing all runtime knobs is powerful but overwhelming; we limit the UI to 3 primary controls with an "Advanced" toggle for expert users. Default presets cover 'Latency-first', 'Cost-first', 'Balanced'.

Guardrails UX: any scenario that increases p99 latency beyond route SLO by >20% shows a caution badge and contains an inline explanation with suggested mitigations (reduce batch size, enable prefix cache, fallback to lower-latency model). If scenario causes estimated token cost increase >50% versus baseline, show blocked state requiring manager approval for rollout.

Rollout integration: each scenario can be saved as a rollout candidate. The design includes a small CTA that converts the selected scenario to a canary rollout config with pre-populated autoscaling floor/ceiling settings.
Accessibility: color contrasts for the traffic-light guardrail badges confirmed; ARIA labels included for interactive sliders; keyboard-only flows for scenario creation validated in wireframes.
decisions: Limit to comparing up to three scenarios simultaneously to keep visual density manageable
Use estimated telemetry model for initial launch; do not require synthetic runs in v1
Require manager approval (explicit checkbox + audit log entry) before enabling scenarios that exceed cost or latency thresholds
Expose presets and expert toggle instead of showing full runtime options by default
review_comments: Grace Kim (PM): 'Love the presets; can we make the baseline selection automatic (most-used config) when opening comparator? Also add a 'Cost per API call' number for business PMs.'

Noah Patel (Eng): 'Simulation API needs a clear contract: include expected latency percentiles and confidence intervals. Also call out performance cost of running scenario evaluations—we should rate-limit or queue them.'
Maya Rao (Security): 'Blocked-state approval flow must create an immutable audit log entry and integrate with SSO identity. Also ensure no PII in scenario payloads.'
Design review (internal): 'Consider adding a compact diff view (only changed metrics) for fast scans in dashboards.'
usability_findings: Initial moderated usability test (5 infra engineers): all completed scenario creation within 4 minutes median time; confusion arose around 'batching window' naming—recommend rename to 'batching latency cap'
Participants requested clearer guidance on when prefix caching is effective; added a contextual tooltip with example query types
Non-engineer PM participant wanted simplified 'one-click recommended scenario' based on current cost+latency targets; added 'Auto-suggest' CTA to scope
handoff_instructions: Component list: ScenarioCard, MetricSeriesChart, PresetToggle, GuardrailBadge, ScenarioDiffView
Telemetry mapping doc: metrics required - token_count, request_qps, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, error_rate, cache_hit_rate, estimated_cost_per_1k_tokens
API contract (v1): POST /api/v1/console/scenario/evaluate -> request: scenario knobs + route id; response: baseline and scenario metrics with confidence band (strings mapping provided in drive doc)
Acceptance tests: visual snapshot of three-pane compare, guardrail badge states, manager approval flow creates audit log entry
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal alpha): Console team + two enterprise customers (opt-in) for one month
Phase 2 (beta): enable for all Dedicated accounts with telemetry opt-in; collect adoption and revert rates
Phase 3 (GA): enabled by default with guardrail thresholds enforced; include analytics card on Console home showing adoption metrics
experiment_metrics: Adoption rate: % of routes using Scenario Comparator within 30 days
Conversion to rollout: % of scenarios applied as canary/rollout
Mean time to decision: time between opening comparator and applying a scenario
Reversion rate: % of rollouts created via comparator that are rolled back within 7 days
False-positive guardrail blocks: count of blocked scenarios later approved by engineering after manual review
timeline: Mar 1 - Mar 8: low-fi flows and presets defined
Mar 9 - Mar 14: hi-fi prototype and microcopy iteration
Mar 15 - Mar 21: engineering handoff and API contract finalization
Mar 22 - Apr 12: internal alpha + telemetry validation
